extracted.intended_audience: grant reviewers, diagnostic assay developers, clinical microbiologists, IRBs and regulatory reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Develop a multiplex, direct-from-CSF FilmArray PCR pouch (FAME) to detect the primary viral and bacterial pathogens of meningoencephalitis, including optimization of sample prep, nested multiplex assay design, and clinical/analytical validation aimed at FDA 510(k) submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for rapid, organism-specific diagnosis
rubrics_metrics.description: A rapid, organism-specific diagnosis is essential for appropriate management of acute meningoencephalitis (ME). Bacterial meningitis and HSV encephalitis are immediately life threatening and must be quickly distinguished from more common aseptic (viral) ME.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale for developing rapid diagnostics: decreases inappropriate antimicrobial therapy, reduces ancillary testing and length of stay, and improves morbidity/mortality. Any diagnostic approach should prioritize speed and organism specificity to change clinical management.

rubrics_metrics.name: CSF sampling via lumbar puncture is mandatory
rubrics_metrics.description: CSF sampling through lumbar puncture (LP) is mandatory for any patient in whom acute ME is suspected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CSF analysis (white cell count, glucose, protein) helps differentiate bacterial vs viral causes, though atypical profiles occur; diagnostic workflows must integrate CSF collection as the canonical specimen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Culture as diagnostic gold standard and limits of culture
rubrics_metrics.description: Culture has long been considered the diagnostic 'gold standard' for CNS infection and is required for antimicrobial susceptibility testing. The sensitivity of CSF bacterial culture is variable (range, 62–85%) and is influenced by prior antibiotic treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design validation comparisons to include culture where possible; acknowledge culture's limited sensitivity and influence by prior antibiotics when interpreting discordant results with molecular methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCR/NAATs as diagnostic modality of choice for viral ME
rubrics_metrics.description: NAATs, specifically PCR, have been shown to bring added value to bacterial Gram stain and culture and are now the diagnostic modality of choice for viral acute ME.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Molecular assays should be central to the diagnostic panel, especially for viral detection, and validated against existing PCR assays and clinical standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiplex simultaneous detection requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Given the number and genetic diversity of potential ME pathogens, several independent PCR tests often need to be combined to cover the spectrum of causative agents; current single-target assays drive up cost and time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A multiplex panel that detects multiple bacterial and viral targets in one run is desirable to reduce time-to-diagnosis and cost. Multiplex design must balance panel breadth with development and regulatory risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform performance characteristics: rapid, integrated, near point-of-care
rubrics_metrics.description: FilmArray is a fully-integrated, automated 'lab-in-a-pouch' system that performs nucleic acid purification, reverse transcription, nested multiplex PCR amplification and target detection for up to 28 targets in about one hour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target product features: fully integrated sample-to-answer workflow, user-friendly operation, self-contained reagents, ~1 hour turnaround, potential availability near point-of-care. Development should preserve these platform advantages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical sensitivity and specificity targets for FDA clearance
rubrics_metrics.description: A clinical sensitivity requirement of at least 90% for each analyte is anticipated for FDA clearance of the FAME panel (the FDA-cleared EV assay from Cepheid achieved 96.3% sensitivity from CSF samples).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and milestone criteria should aim for per-analyte clinical sensitivity ≥90% and high specificity; use comparator assays and published performance benchmarks (e.g., Cepheid EV) when evaluating success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample input volume constraint and need for enrichment
rubrics_metrics.description: FilmArray tests 100 µl of CSF while culture uses 1 mL or more; if sensitivity is limited by low pathogen levels, methods to increase effective volume tested may be needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider pre-enrichment strategies (centrifugation, virus precipitation, concentration) to increase effective sample input 5–10x without meaningfully increasing assay time or complexity; evaluate enrichment tradeoffs (time, biohazard, complexity) and only adopt if justified by sensitivity gain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimize sample purification protocol for CSF
rubrics_metrics.description: FAME panel development will be initiated with the nasopharyngeal swab (NPS) protocol used for the RP panel and will vary FilmArray purification steps (bead beating time, collections on magnetic beads etc.) to optimize for CSF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Cps of amplification curves to monitor purification efficiency and inhibitor removal; compare performance between buffer and CSF matrices; demonstrate equivalent performance before and after optimization (Milestone SA2.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate buffer vs CSF equivalence
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstration that FAME pouch performance is the same with bacteria and virus spiked into buffer and into CSF sample matrix is a milestone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run parallel spiking studies in buffer and in pooled/individual CSF to quantify matrix effects and confirm purification protocol effectiveness; use Cps and limit-of-detection metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development milestone: ~23-assay FAME pouch with comparable performance on spiked CSF
rubrics_metrics.description: Milestone for SA1: Development of a FilmArray pouch with ~23 assays for the pathogens listed, which shows sensitivity and specificity for pathogen detection in spiked CSF comparable to that of existing assays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Iterative assay construction and testing on contrived samples; assays performing less well will be modified/replaced; performance comparable to singleplex/conventional methods is the target.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-enrichment performance goal (LoD reduction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Milestones for SA2 include development of a protocol for pre-enriching the sample that lowers the LoD by five-fold but does not add significant test time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate centrifugation for bacteria, PEG/NaCl precipitation for virus, expected enrichment 5–10x (assuming 50% yield). Reject approaches that add unacceptable time/complexity relative to sensitivity gain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assay primer design principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard issues of primer design: minimally degenerate primers chosen against conserved regions of the bacterial or virus family, Tms around 60 ºC etc are necessary and sufficient to make candidate assays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design outer and inner (nested) primers to balance inclusivity and specificity; target conserved regions across relevant serotypes/strains; maintain uniform cycling conditions where possible to facilitate multiplexing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nested multiplex PCR development workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare the performance of an outer PCR by itself (singleplex) or together with the other outer primers (multiplex) in a block thermocycler with the crossing points (Cps) of the inner, nested, PCR as a readout of the first stage PCR reaction; alter primers as necessary to achieve equivalent performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use inner PCR Cps to infer first-stage multiplex efficiency; iterate primer moves (5' or 3') and primer set selection to equalize performance across assays before committing to the array.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multiple primer sets and array wells for diverse targets
rubrics_metrics.description: The nested format of the PCR and the different wells of the array allow design and assessment of multiple sets of outer and inner primers for pathogens of particular interest; for highly diverse viruses (e.g., enterovirus) evaluate primers with respect to relevant serotypes and CSF-recovered sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For targets with high genetic diversity, include redundant/alternative primer sets and perform sequencing of amplicons from clinical positives to ensure coverage; use literature and in-house sequence data to guide inclusivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparator PCR assays for validation and discrepant resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop one or more 'comparator' PCR assays for the new viruses in the panel, using the literature as a guide; these assays will use hydrolysis or hybridization probe chemistry and will be run in standard real-time PCR instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparator assays serve to confirm FAME positives and resolve discordant results during clinical evaluations; include validated singleplex assays as reference methods in SA3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical testing expectations for Phase II (FDA submission support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase II proposal would outline analytical testing to demonstrate accuracy, reproducibility and robustness of the FAME panel (including studies to determine assay limit of detection, inclusivity, cross-reactivity, sample and reagent storage conditions, and exposure to potential interfering substances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan comprehensive analytical validation experiments (LoD, inclusivity panels, cross-reactivity tests, stability, interfering substances) with pre-specified acceptance criteria to support 510(k) submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical testing plan and sample sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Place FilmArray instruments and FAME pouches with collaborators (PCMC and ARUP) and test de-identified, discarded, pediatric and adult CSF samples; expect to collect 100–150 samples each at PCMC and ARUP for SA3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use frozen residual specimens collected under IRB-approved protocols; run comparator culture/PCR; the FilmArray results will not be provided to clinicians; use adequate sample sizes to estimate sensitivity and specificity per analyte.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation to run comparator assays and resolve discordants
rubrics_metrics.description: We will run comparator PCR assays (developed in SA1) as needed to confirm the FAME result and/or resolve discrepant results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish predefined discrepant resolution algorithms and document confirmation testing; use sequencing or orthogonal assays as necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRB and human subjects protections: de-identification and exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: For ARUP specimens, complete and permanent de-identification of the specimen prior to FilmArray testing qualifies as Exempt Human Research (Exemption 4); accession numbers will be removed and replaced with randomly generated specimen IDs; no PHI will be recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the described de-identification workflow: use accession numbers only to obtain routine lab results, then permanently remove accession numbers and recode; document exemption justification and IRB approvals for non-exempt collections (PCMC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data handling, confidentiality, and HIPAA compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: All clinical and data collection will be performed with IRB approval and comply with HIPAA. Confidentiality will be protected by limiting access to research data and by de-identification of samples tested at ITI; chart abstraction data will be de-identified and PHI-containing records destroyed after abstraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Store results in password-protected databases, share results via secure e-mail, maintain a separate linkage file (secure) if needed, and conduct analyses only on de-identified datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational constraint: results not used for clinical care during development
rubrics_metrics.description: Results from the FilmArray system will not be available in real time and will not be provided to clinicians; therefore this portion is anticipated to be low risk and consent may be waived where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the study so investigational results do not influence patient care and ensure this is documented in IRB protocols and consent waivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel composition governance and SAB oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: The initial panel composition is derived from consultation and literature review; the final composition will be evaluated periodically during development by a Scientific Advisory Board (SAB) of laboratory and medical experts convened by ITI. Larger panels may result in fewer negative results but will increase development and regulatory risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SAB input to balance clinical utility vs development/regulatory burden; document rationale for including/excluding targets and reassess panel size during development milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assay performance threshold for proceeding to Phase II
rubrics_metrics.description: The data collected in SA3 will indicate the likelihood of success for the FAME pouch; for assays not meeting clinical sensitivity targets, consider isolated assay redesign post-Phase I to 'rescue' performance prior to Phase II.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set predefined go/no-go criteria (e.g., per-analyte sensitivity thresholds) and document plans for redesign and additional validation for assays that fail to meet criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target organism list for initial FAME panel
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 3 lists the panel of assays to go into the initial FAME pouch (e.g., Enterobacteriaceae including Escherichia coli, Enterococcus, Haemophilus influenzae, Listeria monocytogenes, Mycoplasma pneumoniae, Neisseria meningitidis, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus species; Enterovirus, Parechovirus, HSV1/2, VZV, EBV, CMV, HHV6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this curated target list as the starting point; adapt composition based on SAB recommendations, epidemiology, and assay inclusivity/cross-reactivity data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain FilmArray platform multiplexing advantages while controlling contamination risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Current multiplex technologies can be labor intensive and prone to laboratory contamination; FilmArray's enclosed nested PCR and array-based second-stage PCR aim to mitigate these issues while enabling high multiplexing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve enclosed, automated workflows to reduce contamination risk; validate that nested format and mechanical hot start maintain sensitivity comparable to singleplex assays while minimizing lab complexity.
